claims.statement: In the FPT/GHEC branch, new organizations start with OAuth app access restrictions enabled, and organization owners may disable them. Creation defaults do not establish present state or permanent enforcement, and owner capability is not authority to weaken restrictions. The pinned product variable means OAuth app, not GitHub App; the linked disabling guide remains separate review work.

The fragment states that pending invitations expire after seven days and release unclaimed licenses. This broad statement must be read alongside the same-pin org-invite-scim fragment's GHEC exception for IdP SCIM-generated invitations; blanket expiry or guaranteed license recovery for all invitations is unsupported. No actual expiry or license-restoration receipt was verified.

An invitation unaccepted after seven days normally expires automatically; the GHEC branch explicitly exempts invitations generated by an IdP SCIM request from expiry. That exception qualifies the separate broad expiry fragment, not every invitation or every IdP workflow; native invitation-origin and expiry behavior remain unverified.
The Organizations list links each organization's Settings entry. This is navigation, not a complete organization inventory, authorized settings access or a verified configuration state.

A sole organization owner creates an availability risk if unreachable; upstream recommends at least two owner-role people per organization. This is advisory source strength, not a platform minimum, mandatory adopted policy, actual redundant ownership or guaranteed recovery. Solo-maintainer capacity and safe alternative recovery need explicit profile-level decisions, not invented second identities or owner grants.
The Access sidebar contains Repository roles. Navigation to role definitions is not assigned users, an effective-permissions census, a complete role matrix or proof of enforcement.
